76-## Rules
77-
78-- Before each WP: `git fetch`; re-verify the plan's finding against current main (other sessions merge in between). If another session already owns the WP's branch, skip to your next WP.
79-- Work in a named worktree per WP (EnterWorktree), branched off origin/main. No stacks. Each worktree builds into its own `target/`, so builds in different worktrees run in parallel with no lock; never run two builds in the same worktree.
80-- Build budget, exported once per session: `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` and `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0` (debug info is most of each `target/`; dropping it cuts disk and link time), `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=$(( $(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) / 4 ))` and the same value for nextest `--test-threads`, so four builders share the CPU.
81-- Mutation testing runs in place in the WP worktree after committing: `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff <diff>`; it reuses the worktree's `target/` instead of copying the tree.
82-- Start independent pieces early in their own worktrees: Session 1 runs G's `pre.json` reader/writer (`model/format/pre.rs`) as a subagent with `isolation: "worktree"` while it works on F1; Session 2 ships J's twine environment change (`runner.rs`) first. Only the parts that touch shared files wait for their chain.
83-- Start the reviewer subagent as soon as the diff is final, in parallel with the gate and mutation run; it reads, it never builds.
84-- When a WP's PR is open and green, `rm -rf <worktree>/target`; after merge, remove the worktree and its local branch.
85-- Fix the root cause by the first rung that works: type or private constructor, exhaustive match, existing lint, one test at the real boundary. Write that test first. Delete checks the type makes redundant. Fix siblings in the same PR.
86-- Specs, ADRs and docs/architecture change in the same PR as behaviour.
87-- Gate by exit code, unsandboxed in the worktree: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, then `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the WP's Rust diff with zero missed (an equivalent mutant gets one line in the PR body).
88-- Design-heavy WPs (L, E, Q): first spawn one Opus subagent (general-purpose, model opus) with the plan's finding and root-cause row; it returns a short design (types, signatures, call sites to migrate, the boundary test). Implement against it yourself.
89-- One fresh-context reviewer per PR (general-purpose, model opus) given only the diff and the finding. Apply what holds up.
90-- Stay at the launched effort; do not escalate unless the same gate failure repeats.
91-- Ship without asking: signed commit, `callisto add` changeset for released-behaviour changes, push, `entire trail ci-pr`. No session links. Never merge.
92-- Ask me only when something requires me: a credential or account, or a plan claim that is false in a way that changes the design.

content.content:
80	## Product gaps from the landscape research
81	
82	- Managed prerelease: owner said yes (crucial for our own releases). Unblocked by R1 + R6; then delete `reject_pre_mode` and E318.
83	- Inferred-only release PRs: falls out of R1 (`PendingRelease` from the post-cascade plan). Opt-in per package through the existing `release-trigger`; no new key. ADR 2 does not forbid it; its consequence bullet and specs `release.json:368`, `cli.json:191` change.
84	- OIDC through native tools, after R7: add `twine` + `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` to `credentials_needed_by` (`runner.rs:82`); `PYPI_TOKEN` optional in init; a pinned `crates-io-auth-action` step feeding `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`; fix `OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md` lines 21, 22, 24. No config key. Tokenless publish stays unproven until run against real registries.
85	- Changesets v2 and v3 migration: R6, then `init` translation of `linked`/`ignore`/`access`/`baseBranch` where an equivalent exists, and a page listing semantic differences (linked groups bump every live member; peer policy; private packages).
86	- Hygiene: delete workspace `tracing`; drop `homepage` (equal to `repository`; Cargo 1.100 warns).
87	
88	## Pushback
89	
90	- No Tokio, plugin framework, trait-per-concern rewrite or execution journal. Every finding is a lost value, a duplicated rule or a shared trust boundary: a type, an index or a job split fixes each.
91	- e18e recommends a protected GitHub Environment with required reviewers. This repo's policy forbids it; R7 gets most of the benefit by keeping `id-token` off every job that runs project code. Binding trusted publishers to an environment stays the owner's call.
92	- No unwrap lint move: measured 806 errors in integration-test helpers; the `justfile` shape works.
93	- No toolchain pin yet: CI's toolchain comes from `orin-dx/actions/setup-rust` (not read). Locally `stable` is 1.98.1, a session override pins 1.99.1, 1.100.0 is current; clippy is clean on 1.100.0.
94	- F06 is lower than the audit's medium: it fails loudly, only with pretty-printed bodies.
95	- No plan-comparison command for migration until its value is measured.
96	- "No ceremony" keeps what the ruleset enforces: signed commits, trails, changesets for released-behaviour fixes, exit-code gates.
97	- AGENTS.md forbids parallel cargo builds. Swarm parallelism is in reading, design and editing; builds take one machine-wide lock. Relaxing that is the owner's call.
98	
99	## Work packages
100	
101	Changeset = fix to released behaviour or a default change.
102	
103	| WP | Scope | Files (overlap risk) | Changeset | Model / effort |
104	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
105	| A | R5 gates + hygiene | `justfile`, `deny.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, bench, `provider/registry/tests.rs` | no | Sonnet, medium |
106	| B | F06 HTTP parser | `provider/http.rs` | yes | Sonnet, medium |
107	| C | F10 typed JSON input | `cli/io.rs`, `cli/commands/release_pr.rs` (args only) | yes | Sonnet, medium |
108	| D | R3 init boundary: `BranchName`, `WorkflowScalar`, `CommitSha` for `__COMMIT__`, F09 hint and E278 help | `graph/commands/init.rs`, templates, `cli/commands/init.rs` | yes | Opus, medium |
109	| E | R2 `NativeName` | `model/identity.rs`, `package_id.rs`, `walk.rs` admission, `identity.rs`, `config/resolve.rs`, `tags.rs`, `release_decision.rs:28-44` | yes | Opus, high |
110	| F1 | R1 `Seed`/`Source` in aggregation | `aggregate.rs`, `cascade.rs`, `version.rs`, `status.rs` | yes (F02) | Opus, high |
111	| F2 | R1 `PendingRelease`, decision `consumed_changesets`, E165 sets; inferred release PRs; F03 | `model/release_pr.rs`, `cli/commands/release_pr.rs`, `release_decision.rs`, `model/release/decision.rs`, action script, ADR 2, specs, `wire-compat.md` | yes | Opus, high |
112	| G | R6 `pre.json` v2/v3 + `pre/` archive | `model/format/pre.rs`, `aggregate.rs` listing, `release_decision.rs` allowed paths, ADR 1 | yes | Opus, medium |
113	| H | Managed prerelease: delete E318, release-PR loop over a pre cycle, lifecycle test | `cli/commands/release_pr.rs`, action script, specs, `errors.md` | yes | Opus, high |

## Product gaps from the landscape research

- Managed prerelease: owner said yes (crucial for our own releases). Unblocked by R1 + R6; then delete `reject_pre_mode` and E318.
- Inferred-only release PRs: falls out of R1 (`PendingRelease` from the post-cascade plan). Opt-in per package through the existing `release-trigger`; no new key. ADR 2 does not forbid it; its consequence bullet and specs `release.json:368`, `cli.json:191` change.
- OIDC through native tools, after R7: add `twine` + `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` to `credentials_needed_by` (`runner.rs:82`); `PYPI_TOKEN` optional in init; a pinned `crates-io-auth-action` step feeding `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`; fix `OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md` lines 21, 22, 24. No config key. Tokenless publish stays unproven until run against real registries.
- Changesets v2 and v3 migration: R6, then `init` translation of `linked`/`ignore`/`access`/`baseBranch` where an equivalent exists, and a page listing semantic differences (linked groups bump every live member; peer policy; private packages).
- Hygiene: delete workspace `tracing`; drop `homepage` (equal to `repository`; Cargo 1.100 warns).

## Pushback

- No Tokio, plugin framework, trait-per-concern rewrite or execution journal. Every finding is a lost value, a duplicated rule or a shared trust boundary: a type, an index or a job split fixes each.
- e18e recommends a protected GitHub Environment with required reviewers. This repo's policy forbids it; R7 gets most of the benefit by keeping `id-token` off every job that runs project code. Binding trusted publishers to an environment stays the owner's call.
- No unwrap lint move: measured 806 errors in integration-test helpers; the `justfile` shape works.
- No toolchain pin yet: CI's toolchain comes from `orin-dx/actions/setup-rust` (not read). Locally `stable` is 1.98.1, a session override pins 1.99.1, 1.100.0 is current; clippy is clean on 1.100.0.
- F06 is lower than the audit's medium: it fails loudly, only with pretty-printed bodies.
- No plan-comparison command for migration until its value is measured.
- "No ceremony" keeps what the ruleset enforces: signed commits, trails, changesets for released-behaviour fixes, exit-code gates.
- AGENTS.md forbids parallel cargo builds. Swarm parallelism is in reading, design and editing; builds take one machine-wide lock. Relaxing that is the owner's call.

## Work packages

Changeset = fix to released behaviour or a default change.

| WP | Scope | Files (overlap risk) | Changeset | Model / effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | R5 gates + hygiene | `justfile`, `deny.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, bench, `provider/registry/tests.rs` | no | Sonnet, medium |
| B | F06 HTTP parser | `provider/http.rs` | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| C | F10 typed JSON input | `cli/io.rs`, `cli/commands/release_pr.rs` (args only) | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| D | R3 init boundary: `BranchName`, `WorkflowScalar`, `CommitSha` for `__COMMIT__`, F09 hint and E278 help | `graph/commands/init.rs`, templates, `cli/commands/init.rs` | yes | Opus, medium |
| E | R2 `NativeName` | `model/identity.rs`, `package_id.rs`, `walk.rs` admission, `identity.rs`, `config/resolve.rs`, `tags.rs`, `release_decision.rs:28-44` | yes | Opus, high |
| F1 | R1 `Seed`/`Source` in aggregation | `aggregate.rs`, `cascade.rs`, `version.rs`, `status.rs` | yes (F02) | Opus, high |
| F2 | R1 `PendingRelease`, decision `consumed_changesets`, E165 sets; inferred release PRs; F03 | `model/release_pr.rs`, `cli/commands/release_pr.rs`, `release_decision.rs`, `model/release/decision.rs`, action script, ADR 2, specs, `wire-compat.md` | yes | Opus, high |
| G | R6 `pre.json` v2/v3 + `pre/` archive | `model/format/pre.rs`, `aggregate.rs` listing, `release_decision.rs` allowed paths, ADR 1 | yes | Opus, medium |
| H | Managed prerelease: delete E318, release-PR loop over a pre cycle, lifecycle test | `cli/commands/release_pr.rs`, action script, specs, `errors.md` | yes | Opus, high |
| I | R4 dir index (F07) + pnpm-relative bench shape | `walk.rs` edges, `manifests/npm.rs`, `fixtures/perf.rs` | yes | Sonnet, high |
| L | R7 publish isolation: pack then publish tarball with `--ignore-scripts`; simple template split into build and publish jobs; attestation job; `id-token` only where needed | `registry_argv.rs`, npm provider, templates, `init.rs`, this repo's release workflow + policy script | yes | Opus, high |
| J | OIDC native (after L) | `cli/runner.rs`, init templates, docs | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| K | Migration v2/v3: init translation + docs | `graph/commands/init.rs` key table, docs | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| M | Changed-without-changeset check (v3 `status --since`) | `status.rs`, `cli.rs` | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| N | Peer default to v3 policy + dev-edge scenario test | `config` defaults, `docs/config.md`, cascade tests | yes (Breaking) | Sonnet, medium |

| Q | Recovery evidence, the positioning claim: a local `just verify-real` harness against local registries (npm verdaccio-style, `cargo-http-registry`, a local PyPI) rehearsing partial publish -> rerun adopts, delayed visibility, conflicting tag, missing Python artifact; production registry binding for Cargo/PyPI (`registry_endpoint.rs` rejects non-https loopback, so the harness needs a test-only allowance decided first); the native install/load matrix recorded from `native_resolution_e2e_tests` | `registry_endpoint.rs`, new harness, docs | no | Opus, high |
| R | Onboarding time and tokenless publish against real registries | needs owner accounts | no | owner + Sonnet |

Investigations (read-only, any time): GH token stripped from native git vs `gh auth git-credential` (needs a clean Linux runner); process-tree cancellation and unbounded output in `run`; multi-distribution prerequisite edges; Sampo head-to-head on one mixed workspace after H.

## Waves

- Wave 0 (now, disjoint files): A, B, C.
- Wave 1: D, E, F1. E and F1 both touch `release_decision.rs` at different ranges: `git merge-tree` before the second merges.
- Wave 2 (critical path, serial): F2 -> G -> H. In parallel: I (after E, shares `walk.rs`), L (after D, shares templates and `init.rs`), N.
- Wave 3: J (after L), K (after G), M (after F2, shares `status.rs`), Q (after E and F2, so it rehearses the fixed model).
- Wave 4: R, then the external pilot.

Critical path: F1 -> F2 -> G -> H. Second chain: D -> L -> J.

## How the swarm runs

- One named worktree per WP, branch off `main`, no stacks; merge in wave order.
- Builds: each worktree has its own target dir; every cargo invocation takes one machine-wide lock (`flock $TMPDIR/callisto-cargo.lock cargo ...`), so agents overlap on thinking and editing, never on builds.
- Per WP: the implementer writes the regression first, driving the real binary or function at the boundary named in the finding, then the type change, then deletes checks the type now covers.
- Proof by exit code: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`; `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the WP diff with zero missed except argued equivalents (it found two real gaps on a caliper branch today); sibling sweep listed in the PR body.
- Review: one fresh-context Opus reviewer per WP, given the diff and the finding, not the implementer's reasoning.
- Gates run unsandboxed in the worktree: sandboxed runs fail tests that write inside the repo and look like defects.
- Ship: signed commit, changeset via `callisto add`, push, link the WP's trail, never create one: #357 Callisto fails predictably (A-E, I); #457 Managed prerelease and inferred release PRs (F1, F2, G, H); #458 Changesets v2 and v3 users can switch (K, M, N); #459 Publish isolation and trusted publishing (L, J); #460 Release recovery evidence (Q, R).
- Orchestration: a Workflow script can run each wave as a pipeline (implement -> mutate -> review -> gate), with the build lock as the only shared resource; it needs an explicit "use a workflow".

## Alpha scope (planning only, not documented)

GitHub-hosted, Linux/macOS, Cargo + npm (napi-rs included), separate-directory Python. Out: Windows, other forges, co-located Maturin, private/HTML PyPI, staged npm publish.

- **Tool provisioning:** a `verify-real-tools` just recipe installs into `target/verify-real/` (a venv plus `cargo install --root`). The CI action calls that recipe, so the pins live in one place.
- Locally I found only npx, uv, python3 and openssl. verdaccio, pypiserver, twine and cargo-http-registry are all missing, so the provisioning step is required.

**(c) Where the harness lives and how each scenario runs**
- **Justfile:** `verify-real: verify-real-tools` → `cargo test -p callisto-cli --test release_verify_real -- --ignored --test-threads=1` with the tools prepended to PATH.
- **Test file:** `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_verify_real.rs`, `#![cfg(unix)]`. Each test is `#[ignore = "needs local registries; run via just verify-real"]`. A missing tool panics rather than skipping (unlike `skip_missing`, :282), so any wrong outcome gives a nonzero exit. All logic stays in Rust; the shell only provisions tools.
- **Harness change:** add `real_publishers()` to release_harness.rs. It reuses the fake `git` (push plus the remote-tag store, release_harness.rs:546,1215-1232) and the fake `gh`, but writes no fake `cargo` (fake_publishers writes one, :535-541).
- **New `execute_real()`:** like `execute` (:574-608) but without `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=REDACTED or `CALLISTO_TEST_CARGO_MARKER`. It sets the CA variables, `TWINE_USERNAME`/`TWINE_PASSWORD`, `CARGO_HOME` (holding the `.cargo` config and token) and `__CALLISTO_TEST_SLEEP_SCALE=0.1`. The origin stays `https://github.com/...` (:183), which passes the git-remote rule.
- **Scenario 0 (proves the binding is production):** the same workspace with `url = "http://127.0.0.1:<port>"` fails with E126 before any effect (spec docs/specs/release.json:222).
- **(1) Partial publish, then rerun adopts:** npm packages `a` and `b`, where `b` depends on `a`. They bind to two npm-kind `[registries]` entries, each its own TLS verdaccio. In run 1, `b`'s registry is not started, so the run fails and writes no receipt. Run 2 starts it and must:
  - exit 0 and write a receipt;
  - show `a ... is already published; skipping` on stderr (spec :285);
  - leave registry 1 with `a` exactly once and registry 2 with `b`.
  - The cargo variant: crate `core` bound to a key-only `local-e2e` entry whose `.cargo` config points at a port not yet listening in run 1.
- **(2) Delayed visibility:** PyPI split routes. `url` is index server I (`https://127.0.0.1:I/simple`), `publish-url` is upload server U (spec :235), each a pypiserver on its own directory. A test thread copies U's directory into I's after about 3 s. With `confirm-timeout = "30s"`, the run must succeed after more than one look (spec :239). A variant that never copies must exit with E157 and no receipt; a rerun after the copy adopts.
- **(3) Conflicting tag:** seed `$CALLISTO_TEST_GIT_TRACE.remote-tags` with `<pkg>@<ver>` pointing at another object. The run must exit with E167, write no receipt, and never adopt the tag (spec :293). Whether the registry is untouched depends on when tags are checked relative to effects; read that ordering from the code at implementation time.
- **(4) Missing Python artifact:** seed index directory I (or U and I together) with the sdist only. Then `release execute` must upload just the wheel, end with both files on the index, and leave the sdist unchanged. Twine never passes `--skip-existing` (registry_argv.rs:366-372), so if callisto re-uploaded the sdist, pypiserver would refuse it and the run would fail. Success itself proves only the missing file was sent.

**(d) Files, tests and docs**
- **Production code:** none. The boundary tests stay unchanged: registry_endpoint.rs:124 (http rejected, loopback included) and :141 (https accepted).
- **New:**
  - `tests/release_verify_real.rs`
  - `tests/common/local_registries.rs`
  - `real_publishers` / `execute_real` in `tests/common/release_harness.rs`
  - justfile `verify-real` and `verify-real-tools` recipes
  - action.yml calls `just verify-real-tools`.
- **Edit release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs:12-34:** its header says a loopback registry "can never be configured", which TLS now makes false. Repoint it at the shared helpers. Optional, owner's call: delete its argv-level PyPI and cargo tests as superseded and run `just verify-real` in the Linux CI job instead.
- **Docs:**
  - AGENTS.md Commands: one bullet for `just verify-real`.
  - docs/architecture/release.md: one line naming the rehearsal and the local-TLS approach.
  - docs/specs: no change. The harness is not product behavior, and release.json:222 stays true.
- **Changeset:** none (not user-visible), as the plan says.

**Risks to spike first, all cheap:**
- macOS curl honoring `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`.
- twine honoring `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`.
- The `pypiserver:app` keyword arguments under gunicorn.
- verdaccio's https config.
- Execution order in scenario (1), i.e. that `a` is issued before `b` fails. Check that callisto orders npm packages by dependency.

For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.

Example:
```toml
[registries.internal-npm]
kind = "npm"
url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
```

## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`

Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact ecosystem-qualified id: the package's own name in that ecosystem, which for a dual package can differ per ecosystem (first matching rule wins). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is an ecosystem-qualified glob, compared with each package's name in that ecosystem, and can match many packages at once; a rule for several ecosystems is one rule per ecosystem; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact `ecosystem/name`. `[[package-set]]`: `ecosystem/glob`. The ecosystem is `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; a name without one is E317. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

test:
    name: Test Suite (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@c509219cf42fba86913069efd0ade2458c59337b # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@c509219cf42fba86913069efd0ade2458c59337b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest
      - name: Install workflow linters
        uses: $/.github/actions/install-workflow-linters
      - name: Install registry test tools
        uses: $/.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools
      - run: just test
      - run: just release-workflow-behavior
      - name: Verify Release-PR action against the real callisto binary
        run: bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh
      - name: Verify the problem matcher against the real callisto error
        run: bash .github/tests/test-problem-matcher.sh

  release-artifact-preflight:
    name: Release Artifact Preflight (${{ matrix.id }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: macos-arm64
            runner: macos-latest
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@c509219cf42fba86913069efd0ade2458c59337b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Install registry test tools
        uses: $/.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools

name: 'Install registry test tools'
description: 'Installs the local npm, PyPI and Cargo registries the real-registry e2e tests run against. Linux only; the tests fail without them under CI.'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Verdaccio (real-registry npm e2e coverage)
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      shell: bash
      run: npm install -g verdaccio@6.10.4 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.
    - name: Install pypiserver (real-registry PyPI e2e coverage)
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      shell: bash
      # legacy-cgi: pypiserver imports `cgi` (gone in 3.13). gunicorn: avoids a slow getfqdn() bind.
      # setuptools/wheel: the test builds with `--no-isolation`, so they must be pre-installed.
      run: | # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not attacker-controlled input.
        python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv"
        "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin/pip" install pypiserver==2.4.0 twine==6.2.0 build==1.4.4 legacy-cgi==2.6.3 gunicorn==26.2.0 setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1
        echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
    - name: Install cargo-http-registry (real-registry Cargo e2e coverage)
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      shell: bash
      run: cargo install --locked cargo-http-registry@0.1.8 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.

# gunicorn: pypiserver's default backend does a slow getfqdn() bind. setuptools and wheel: the offline Python build.
verify-real-tools:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    tools=target/verify-real
    mkdir -p "$tools"
    npm install --silent --no-audit --no-fund --prefix "$tools/npm" verdaccio@6.10.4
    if command -v uv >/dev/null; then uv venv -q --allow-existing --python 3.12 "$tools/venv"; else python3 -m venv "$tools/venv"; fi
    python_pins="pypiserver==2.4.0 twine==6.2.0 build==1.4.4 legacy-cgi==2.6.3 gunicorn==26.2.0 setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1"
    "$tools/venv/bin/python" -m pip install -q $python_pins
    "$tools/venv/bin/python" -m pip download -q -d "$tools/wheels" setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1
    cargo install --locked --root "$tools/cargo" cargo-http-registry@0.1.8

set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]

# Default recipe: fast local CI pipeline (no coverage) via moon & just.
# Use `just ci` explicitly for full CI parity including coverage.
default: ci

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:
    moon run :build

# Build release CLI binary
build-release:
    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli

# Time `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and count their git processes.
# `CALLISTO_BENCH_PACKAGES=50,200` picks the sizes.
bench:
    cargo bench -p callisto-cli --bench commands

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests. This intentionally uses the
# same Nextest command as CI: a runner/configuration failure must never be
# mistaken for a passing Moon fallback.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Explicit compatibility path for contributors who do not have cargo-nextest
# installed. It is never used by CI or pre-merge verification.
test-moon:
    moon run :test
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Exercise the Release-PR action's shell block with Git and GitHub faked; it never calls the real binary (see test-release-action-binary).
test-release-action:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and runs the Release-PR action's jq extraction against
# its real JSON output. Requires pending changesets to exercise update and
# supersede decisions; skips cleanly otherwise.
test-release-action-binary:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and feeds its real error output through the CI problem matcher.
test-problem-matcher:
    bash .github/tests/test-problem-matcher.sh

# Execute the release lifecycle at the real CLI boundary with fake registry,
# Git, forge, and attestation providers. This is deliberately separate from
# broad workspace tests so PR CI makes the release behavior evidence visible.
release-workflow-behavior:
    bash .github/tests/release-workflow-behavior/run.sh

# Re-captures the real provider responses under testing/fixtures/providers with
# read-only network GETs. Manual: review the diff and update PROVENANCE.md.
provider-fixtures:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh

# Manual and network-dependent, so deliberately not part of `ci`: re-fetches the
# live providers and asserts each fixture's SHAPE (status code, JSON key paths,
# ls-remote line kinds) still matches; content is never compared.
provider-contract:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh --check

# Reject history words and plain comment blocks over three lines (`comment-block-ok` marks an exception).
check-comments:
    bash testing/check-comments.sh

# Clippy as one workspace invocation: moon's per-project runs serialize on cargo's shared target/ lock.
lint: check-comments
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used

# Lint only moon-affected projects, in one cargo invocation to avoid the build-lock serialization.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used

# Check code formatting compliance via moon
fmt-check:
    moon run :format-check

# Format code automatically via moon
fmt:
    moon run :format

# Security advisory, ban, license & source check via cargo-deny (workspace root, one pass)
audit: license-boundary
    cargo deny check

# callisto-model is MIT: nothing it depends on at build or run time, directly or not, may be FSL-licensed or a Callisto FSL crate.
license-boundary:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    tree=$(cargo tree -p callisto-model -e normal,build --prefix none --format '{p} {l}')
    if [ -z "$tree" ]; then echo "cargo tree printed nothing" >&2; exit 1; fi
    if grep -E 'FSL|callisto-(manifests|graph|cli|fixtures)' <<<"$tree"; then exit 1; fi

# Compile the fuzz targets so they cannot rot (running them needs nightly and cargo-fuzz)
fuzz-check:
    cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins

# Run mutation testing sweep via cargo-mutants
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# The shipped binary is built with the features its crates default to, and none of them is the dev-only `test-util`.
features-boundary:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    tree=$(cargo tree -p callisto-cli -e normal,build -f '{p} {f}')
    if [ -z "$tree" ]; then echo "cargo tree printed nothing" >&2; exit 1; fi
    if grep 'test-util' <<<"$tree"; then exit 1; fi

# Run unused dependency check via cargo-machete
machete:
    cargo machete

# Verify public Rust API SemVer breaking changes
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Run structure-aware fuzzing target
fuzz target="parse_package_id":
    cargo fuzz run {{target}}

# Documentation build check (warnings treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace

# Coverage via cargo-llvm-cov; a `threshold` fails below that line coverage, after printing the summary.
# `just ci` and CI both call `just coverage 90`, so a CI failure reproduces locally.
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    args=(--workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info)
    cargo llvm-cov "${args[@]}"
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{threshold}}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{threshold}}"
    fi

# Per-crate line coverage against a threshold (default 90%): the workspace total can pass while a small crate is far below.
# Needs profile data from a prior `cargo llvm-cov` run; it does not re-run tests.
coverage-per-crate threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    summary=$(mktemp)
    trap 'rm -f "$summary"' EXIT
    cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only > "$summary"
    report=$(jq -r '
        .data[0].files[]
        | select(.filename | test("/crates/"))
        | {crate: (.filename | capture("/crates/(?<c>[^/]+)/").c), count: .summary.lines.count, covered: .summary.lines.covered}
        | [.crate, .count, .covered]
        | @tsv
      ' "$summary" \
      | awk -F'\t' -v threshold="{{threshold}}" '
          {sum[$1]+=$2; cov[$1]+=$3}
          END {
            for (c in sum) {
              pct = (cov[c]/sum[c]*100)
              status = (pct+0 < threshold+0) ? "FAIL" : "pass"
              printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%.2f\t%s\n", c, sum[c], cov[c], pct, status
            }
          }
        ' | sort)
    if [ -z "$report" ]; then echo "no per-crate coverage data: run cargo llvm-cov first" >&2; exit 1; fi
    echo "$report" | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%-25s lines=%-6s covered=%-6s cover=%6s%%  %s\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5}'
    if grep -q FAIL <<<"$report"; then exit 1; fi

# Clean build targets, Moon task caches, and generated artifacts
clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean
    rm -f lcov.info callisto-schema.json

# Fast pre-commit hook validation (<500ms formatting check)
pre-commit: fmt-check

# Pre-push hook validation: formatting check plus clippy on affected projects only
pre-push: fmt-check lint-affected

# Install native Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks
hooks:
    @printf '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-commit\n' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @printf '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-push\n' > .git/hooks/pre-push
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push
    @echo "Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks installed successfully."

# Static security audit of workflows and actions (requires zizmor and ripgrep).
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Credential-free release workflow contract, policy, and policy mutant checks.
release-workflow-checks:
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh

# Workflow Contracts CI job minus actionlint and zizmor: pins, release
# contract/policy, artifact build script, the Release-PR action contract
# under a minimal PATH, and the installer verification-mode tests.
workflow-contracts: release-workflow-checks
    bash .github/tests/test_release_candidate_recovery.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-release-artifact-build-script.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-move-floating-tag.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-hold-release-pr.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_contract.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_download_extraction_format.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_action_ref_version_resolution.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_crates_io_fallback.sh

# Every check CI runs except actionlint (Docker) and the binary-dependent
# release-PR decide contract, problem matcher contract and artifact preflight build. CI runs them as
# parallel jobs (callisto-ci.yml); locally they run in sequence.
ci: fmt-check lint fuzz-check test audit doc-check zizmor workflow-contracts release-workflow-behavior (coverage "90")

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Before every push or PR: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, and `just ci` before marking a PR ready. Judge each by its exit code. Never tail or grep the output for success (a compile error prints no "failed" line), and never report a check as passed that was not run.
- Commits must be signed: the ruleset requires it. Never pass `-c commit.gpgsign=false`. After pushing, `gh api repos/orin-dx/callisto/commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.reason` must say `valid`.
- Performance: `just bench` times `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and counts the git processes each starts (`CALLISTO_BENCH_SHAPES=1` lists which). A change that adds a git process per package fails review.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel in the same checkout.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Changesets

- Write one with `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic. A fix to something not yet released has no changeset.
- Changesets become the project's changelog, so write them for the people who use it, not for the implementer.
- Open with a bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it, then one line on its value: what they can now do or what changed for them.
- When there is more to say, add short bullets in this order: why it matters, how to adopt it (commands, configuration, migration), and limits they will hit. Use sub-bullets for detail.
- Group a longer entry under bold labels such as **Upgrading** or **Scripting**. Do not use `#` headings; the changelog supplies those.
- Put a breaking change in its own paragraph starting `**Breaking:**` (old behavior, new behavior, what to do), and a step users must take in one starting `**Action:**`. Never inside a bullet: the release PR lists them under "Read before merging" only as paragraphs.
- One idea per bullet. Leave out internals unless the user must know them.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON changes that only replace string values are written into the original text by span (`json_text`), anything else keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Enforcing an invariant

Use the first rung that works:

1. A type, or a private constructor or field, so the wrong thing cannot compile.
2. An exhaustive `match` with no `_` arm on our own enums.
3. A clippy or rustc lint already in the workspace lints.
4. One small test that drives the real binary or function and checks observable behavior.
5. Nothing.

- No tests that scan source text, or grep docs or workflows for strings that code can expose directly.
- No hand-maintained lists that mirror code (error codes, command names, env names): derive them from the type.
- Prefer a crate already in `Cargo.lock` over a hand-written grammar: `semver` for versions, `miette` and `thiserror` for errors, `clap` derive for args, `serde` for formats, `insta` for snapshots.
- Every new error code, JSON key or flag is permanent after 1.0: prefer fewer, broader ones.
- Before adding a check, delete one that a type now covers.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Plugins

Start work through these commands so their checks run: `/wisp:explore` (options before deciding), `/wisp:spike` (does it work), `/wisp:fix` (bug or review findings), `/wisp:build` (real feature or shared change), `/wisp:check` (verify or find bugs), `/wisp:ship` (commit, changeset, PR, release). `/wisp:work` picks one when unsure.

Packs: rust-house

Changesets are written with `callisto add` and follow the changeset rules in this file. `/wisp:build` writes a spec only where one pays; the owner-confirmation rule below still applies.

Pull requests are opened by Entire from the branch's trail: push the branch and create or link its trail (`entire trail create`). Do not open the PR with `gh`.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- A commit or PR may end with the `Claude-Session:` trailer. Keep claude.ai session links out of source and documentation files.

content.text:
WP Q is pushed as PR #572 (trail #460), but `just verify-real` only covers npm and PyPI. Cargo can't be rehearsed.

`just verify-real` exits 0 with 5 of 5 rehearsals passing. `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test` each exited 0 on the final tree, and so did `just workflow-contracts`. I did not run `just ci`, mutation testing (the diff has no production Rust) or the CI action change on a real runner.

**How it gets past the https rule:** I changed no production code. The local registries serve a self-signed `https://127.0.0.1` certificate, and npm, curl and Twine trust it through their own CA variables. `[registries.npm]` and `[registries.pypi]` therefore bind through the production binding unchanged. The existing test that rejects http, loopback included, still passes.

**What the rehearsals cover:**
- **Partial npm publish:** the registry refuses the second package, then the rerun adopts the first and finishes.
- **PyPI index shows the upload late:** the run waits and succeeds, and the test asserts the index served a 404 first.
- **PyPI index never shows the upload:** the run fails with E157, and a rerun after the index catches up adopts it without re-uploading.
- **Conflicting tag:** the run fails with E167.
- **PyPI index missing one built file:** only the missing wheel is uploaded.

**What it cannot do:**
- **No Cargo rehearsal:** callisto always passes `--registry crates-io`, and cargo sends that publish to the real crates.io API even when the source is replaced. My probe hit crates.io with a fake token and got a 401. Documented in AGENTS.md and `docs/architecture/release.md`. Rehearsing Cargo would take a production change that lets a package name a custom Cargo registry, which is your call.

## Where a publish goes

A registry with no `url` in `callisto.toml` publishes wherever the checkout's own configuration says: `.npmrc` for npm and `.cargo/config.toml` for Cargo. Callisto honors that on purpose, so a private registry set there keeps working, and it means those files decide where the registry token is sent. Review changes to them like code. A release pull request cannot carry such a change: a version commit may only touch manifests, lockfiles, changelogs, changesets and the decision file, and any other path fails verification with E165. For npm (except yarn) and PyPI, set `url` on the registry entry to pin the destination in `callisto.toml`; Cargo takes its destination only from `.cargo/config.toml`, and a `url` on a cargo registry is rejected.

   - Result: a user following the docs runs the release with no credential, and the publish fails with an auth error at execute time.

5. **Minor gap in what the tests prove.** `release_hardening_tests.rs:1050-1072` checks the publish and observation command lines only. Nothing covers a confirm-timeout or publish-timeout set on a named registry (wired through `binding.rs:117-118`), or the fingerprint for that target.

content.text:
Part 1 is up as PR #575 (trail #460). Part 2 is not started; it waits for #575 to merge, as you specified.

A `[registries.<name>]` entry with `kind = "cargo"` is now a valid `publish-to` target. `cargo publish` and `cargo info` both receive `--registry <name>`, and `.cargo/config.toml` resolves the URL. A `url` on a cargo registry is still rejected with E336.

- **Checks:** `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test` all exited 0. `cargo mutants --in-diff` reports 0 missed (16 caught, 6 unviable). The first run missed 3 mutants, so I added a unit test for the new variant.
- **Tests:** the boundary tests were written first and failed first. They drive the real binary and show `publish` and `info` naming `--registry my-reg` with no `crates-io`. They also cover E336 on a `url`, and E330 for an unknown name, a non-cargo registry and `cratesIo`.
- **No new codes or keys:** only the registry `kind` was used. The only code touched is E330, whose help text and `docs/errors.md` row now mention registry names. `PublishTarget` gained a `CargoRegistry` variant and `config_str()` now returns `&str`. Wire output for `crates-io` is unchanged.
- **Docs and changeset:** fixed `docs/publishing.md:38` and updated `docs/config.md`, REL-PUB-06 and REL-PUB-18. I added a `callisto add` changeset (cargo/callisto-cli minor).
- **Commit and push:** signed, GitHub reports `valid`, no session trailer. `git ls-remote` matches `a5a5d0b21746`. The fresh Opus reviewer's findings are addressed below.

**Review findings, handled and deferred:**
- **Fixed:** a malformed registry name (such as `my.reg`) now fails at load with E330 instead of late with E159.
- **Fixed:** the docs and changeset now say the release job needs `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN`.
- **Documented, not fixed:** the built-in target names (`none`, `github-release`, `npm` and so on) always mean the built-in target, even if a cargo registry is declared under that name. Rejecting them would need a new code, so I did not add one.
- **Corrected a claim of mine:** a `crates-io` publish runs plain `cargo publish` with no `--registry`, while observation passes `--registry crates-io`. Cargo's own config can therefore redirect the publish, and Callisto then fails with E157 after the upload. This predates the PR and I left the behaviour alone. `publishing.md` now says so. My earlier AGENTS.md line in #572, "callisto always publishes with `--registry crates-io`", is wrong and gets fixed in part 2.
- **Not covered by tests:** `confirm-timeout`/`publish-timeout` on a named registry, and the fingerprint for that target. The fingerprint arm is exercised by the boundary test, but nothing pins its value.

Decision for you: should a cargo registry named like a built-in target (`none`, `github-release` and so on) be rejected at config load? It needs a new error code, so I held off.

I deleted the worktree's `target/`. Once #575 merges, tell me and I'll start part 2: the Cargo rehearsals and the native install/load matrix in #572.

name: 'Install registry test tools'
description: 'Installs the local npm, PyPI and Cargo registries the real-registry e2e tests run against, through `just verify-real-tools`. Linux only; the tests fail without them under CI.'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install the local registries
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      shell: bash
      run: | # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entries are fixed children of the checkout, not attacker-controlled input.
        just verify-real-tools
        for dir in venv/bin npm/node_modules/.bin cargo/bin; do
          echo "$PWD/target/verify-real/$dir" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        done
    if [ -z "$tree" ]; then echo "cargo tree printed nothing" >&2; exit 1; fi
    if grep 'test-util' <<<"$tree"; then exit 1; fi

# The local npm, PyPI and Cargo registries the real-registry suites run against, installed under target/verify-real.
# gunicorn: pypiserver's default backend does a slow getfqdn() bind. setuptools and wheel: the offline Python build.
verify-real-tools:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    for tool in npm pnpm uv; do
        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || { echo "$tool is required: the install matrix uses npm, pnpm and uv" >&2; exit 1; }
    done
    tools=target/verify-real
    mkdir -p "$tools"
    npm install --silent --no-audit --no-fund --prefix "$tools/npm" verdaccio@6.10.4
    uv venv -q --seed --allow-existing --python 3.12 "$tools/venv"
    python_pins="pypiserver==2.4.0 twine==6.2.0 build==1.4.4 legacy-cgi==2.6.3 gunicorn==26.2.0 setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1"
    "$tools/venv/bin/python" -m pip install -q $python_pins
    "$tools/venv/bin/python" -m pip download -q -d "$tools/wheels" setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1
    cargo install --locked --root "$tools/cargo" cargo-http-registry@0.1.8

# Rehearses recovery against local npm, PyPI and Cargo registries, then runs the native install matrix.
verify-real: verify-real-tools
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    tools="$PWD/target/verify-real"
    export PATH="$tools/venv/bin:$tools/npm/node_modules/.bin:$tools/cargo/bin:$PATH"
    cargo --version && npm --version && pnpm --version && uv --version
    VERIFY_REAL_WHEELS="$tools/wheels" cargo test -p callisto-cli --test release_verify_real -- --ignored --test-threads=1
    cargo test -p callisto-cli --test native_resolution_e2e_tests -- --test-threads=1
